title: Peas, green, sweet, canned, sodium added, sugar added, drained and rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Green canned peas are mature pod peas harvested at full size, blanched, canned in a brine with added salt and sugar, then drained and rinsed. They retain a bright green color, a mildly sweet flavor, and a firm texture, making them convenient for quick meals and long‑term storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned peas are a staple in many cuisines, from classic American pea soup to Indian dal.
Adding salt and sugar enhances flavor and helps preserve the peas' color and texture during storage.
Peas belong to the legume family, which can fix atmospheric nitrogen, improving soil fertility.
Draining and rinsing after canning reduces sodium content, making the product more suitable for low‑salt diets.
Green peas are rich in plant protein, dietary fiber, and B‑vitamins.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned peas provides about 8 g of protein, making it a valuable protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamins and minerals
items.content: Peas contain vitamins C, K, B6, and minerals such as iron, magnesium, and phosphorus.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Despite the added sugar, peas have a moderate glycemic index, which can be compatible with blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients like flavonoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even after rinsing, the product may still contain notable amounts of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, including peas.

items.title: Bisphenol A in cans
items.content: Canned goods can contain trace amounts of BPA; choose BPA‑free labeled products when possible.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: The added sugar increases calorie count and may be undesirable for low‑sugar diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add peas to soups, stews, salads, pasta dishes, or side dishes. They can be quickly heated in the microwave or sautéed with a little oil and seasonings. For a fresher taste, rinse them with cold water before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep peas in an airtight container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑4 days. Discard if they develop an off‑odor or discoloration.
